stemMd: Which statement correctly distinguishes the light reactions of photosynthesis from carbon fixation?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Carbon fixation directly splits water to release oxygen.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Only carbon fixation requires any enzymes.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The light reactions produce ATP and NADPH used in carbon fixation.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Carbon fixation occurs only in animal mitochondria.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The light reactions consume glucose as their only energy source.

explanationMd: The light reactions convert light energy into chemical forms, including ATP and NADPH, and release oxygen from water. Carbon-fixation reactions use that chemical energy and reducing power to incorporate carbon dioxide into organic compounds. The stages are linked but perform distinct tasks.

distractorRationale.a: Water splitting belongs to the light reactions.
distractorRationale.b: Both stages involve enzymes and other proteins.
distractorRationale.e: Light provides the energy captured in these reactions.
distractorRationale.d: In plants it occurs in the chloroplast stroma.
